source.title: Ground-truth evaluation of sparse autoencoder features on spatial, single-cell and language-model embeddings
source.authors: Amirhossein Shahsavand; Shayan Forghani; Saba Akbarzadeh; Fatemeh Mahdavi Sabet

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE features align with known concepts and reproduce across fits, and finds limits to their stability and coverage. It does not test the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: Rows cover measured SAE concept coverage and reproducibility relevant to LLM dictionary features and their completeness or stability. The study does not measure feature overlap geometry, orthogonality, interference, neuron polysemanticity, or feature dimensionality. It also reports cited prior results, kNN identity accuracy, and biological gene-program purity; these are not recorded as rows for the tested claim versions.
record.test_reason: On the Pythia-70m residual stream, and on Geneformer as a second neural model, the study measures whether SAE features recover known concepts (V4, V5 completeness) and whether they recur across refits (V5 stability). Its results qualify V5: single fits are seed-dependent, and consensus stability depends on dictionary size and data amount. Most other rows are PCA or other non-LLM embeddings of transcriptomic data, which are not a neural model's representation.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct, but incomplete. The authors conclude that reproducibility alone ranks features poorly. SAE features should be reported with concept coverage and purity, against a rotation sparsified to the SAE's sparsity. A five-seed consensus makes features reproducible and keeps them pure, but it covers fewer lineages than single fits, and all SAEs miss weak planted states that rotations recover. What the consensus discards is mostly seed-specific detail. Reproducibility values depend on the embedding and the amount of data, so thresholds should not be carried across domains.
record.recipe_differences: Uses BatchTopK and Matryoshka SAEs, consensus matching across seeds, and concept-ground-truth comparisons with rotation baselines; it does not reproduce the Toy Models of Superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reproducibility varied by source (78% on Pythia-70m versus 85–98% across the other reported sources), dictionary size, and amount of token data. Recovery of planted states varied by state strength and sequencing depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Rotation features of the Pythia residual stream are perfectly reproducible (R1 1.00) yet cover only 1 of 8 token classes (varimax). Sparse varimax covers 6.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-seed reproducibility of a decomposition does not indicate that its features align with concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: On PCA-embedded planted data, SAEs recover no more programs than rotations. SAEs spend several features on strong lineages and miss mid and weak states that varimax recovers (consensus 0.28 vs varimax 0.61 weak).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionaries allocate latents by explained variance, duplicating strong concepts and missing weak ones (non-neural embeddings).

fits_no_version.finding: On spatial transcriptomic embeddings, the consensus raises reproducibility to 92–98% but covers 2–5 of 7 lineages, fewer than single fits (up to 6.7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Consensus filtering trades concept coverage for reproducibility in SAEs on non-LLM embeddings.

record.problems: The authors note narrow ground truth, two SAE variants, models up to 70 million parameters, and spatial data from two sections of one cancer type. Most configurations used three seeds. Some reported ranges are aggregate ranges rather than source-specific values.
record.rows_left_out: Left out biological gene-program purity and Hallmark enrichment, kNN identity accuracy, runtime comparisons, and detailed residual-stage and longer-fit results; these do not directly measure the versions recorded here. Per-embedding spatial values are not separately given in the main text for every metric.

untested.parts: No toy-model geometry, overlap, orthogonality, interference or sparsity transition is tested.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation in neurons is measured.
No alternative origins of polysemantic neurons are tested.
Spread of features across neurons is not measured, and no LLM larger than Pythia-70m is studied. Only one layer (3) and eight rule-defined token classes are used.
Untested: completeness beyond eight token classes and seven lineages; canonicality across models, sizes, layers or training stages; Pythia-specific single-fit reproducibility.
No comparison of 1-D directions with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Geneformer is kept on V5 as a transformer model's representation; V4 is limited to Pythia-70m. Consensus reproducibility is partly built in, since it keeps only features that recur across seeds. Reproducibility on Pythia is lower than on the biological sources, which the authors link to the embedding's higher effective dimension (about 70 vs 8.5–20).

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy-network superposition geometry, overlap, orthogonality, interference, or sparsity-dependent transitions.
Does not measure neuron polysemanticity or whether features compete for neuron dimensions according to importance.
Does not test polysemantic neurons arising through other mechanisms.
Tests SAE recovery of rule-defined token classes in Pythia-70m, not feature spread across neurons or feature recovery in larger LLMs.
Tests coverage of selected known concepts and reproducibility across fits. Does not establish completeness for all concepts or canonicality across tasks, models, or training stages.
Does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional feature subspaces.
